newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, window-dressing seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, window-dressing seen.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly flat in early Tuesday trade, with some firming on year-end window-dressing, dealers said.
"Volume is very thin on higher prices, reflecting that this is not a broad base activity. Some window-dressing are pushing up certain stocks," said a dealer.
"But in general, people have stopped trading for the year," she added.
At 0215 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index eased 6.89 points to 2,211.56. Volume was a paltry 16 million shares, with gainers leading decliner by 93 to 71.
Malaysia's Promet Bhd led the actives with 1.8 million shares following news on Monday that property company Berjaya Industrial Bhd had bought a 17 percent stake in the maritime and engineering firm.
Dealers said the purchase of 100 million Promet shares was worth 3.50 ringgit each, or about S$1.96. Promet shares traded over the counter in Singapore rose S$0.06 to S$1.22.
Chemical Industries saw 1.377 million of its 1.39 million shares crossed at S$3.08. It was up S$0.10 to S$3.30.
Multimedia Creative Technology rose S$0.50 to S$14.60 while UOB Foreign fell S$0.30 to S$15.60.
